channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Hark launches this week: Brett Adcock promises the first 100,000 users a free paid plan
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Brett Adcock says Hark, the $700M-backed personal-AI lab he seeded with $100M of his own money, launches its first product this week — and the first 100,000 registered users get the paid plan free.

item.title: SCM brings local AI search to every photo — and every video frame — on your Mac
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SCM (Screen Memories) is an open-source macOS app that indexes any folder of photos and videos entirely on-device — CLIP/SigLIP vision search, Tesseract OCR in 36+ languages, Whisper transcripts, and an opt-in local LLM. It hit Hacker News today.

item.title: Anthropic whistleblower Jacob Coxon will testify at NYC's AI hearing Monday — Bloomberg
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bloomberg reported Sunday that Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic researcher who quit last month warning AI labs are 'gambling with our lives,' will testify Monday at a New York City Council AI hearing — at Speaker Julie Menin's request, as lawmakers weigh a package of safety bills.

item.title: Run a 125-billion-parameter model on your own gaming PC: hands-on with Strata
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strata (Niko1221/Strata, 11,000+ stars in ten days, MIT) runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — a 125-billion-parameter model — on a gaming PC with 12 GB of VRAM and 32 GB of RAM. One-click install, an OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8080, and about 53 tokens per second on an RTX 5070. Here’s the hardware check, the model sizes, and how to point your coding agents at it.

item.title: Is your model getting quietly worse? Build a daily LLM drift monitor — the livenerf playbook
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: livenerf (ninjahawk/livenerf, 1,200+ stars, MIT) asks whether frontier models quietly get worse after launch — and turned the argument into a 30-day experiment with a day-0 baseline. Steal the playbook: freeze a discriminating question panel, run it daily on your model with Inspect, and catch drift with statistics instead of vibes.

item.title: Axios: Nvidia-backed Reflection is about to release its first open-weight model — America’s answer to Chinese open weights
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Axios reported Sunday that Reflection — the startup founded by DeepMind alumni, valued at $8B with Nvidia as its biggest backer — is preparing its first open-weight model, aimed squarely at China’s open-weight leaders, and has been pitching its ‘AI factory’ vision in Washington.

item.title: Trump launches the Super Intelligence Force: DNI Jay Clayton leads, with the FTC's Ferguson, the Pentagon's Emil Michael, and OPM's Kupor
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: President Trump announced the Super Intelligence Force's leadership in a Sunday Truth Social post: DNI Jay Clayton chairs the task force alongside FTC chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon CTO Emil Michael, and OPM director Scott Kupor — with 120 days to produce a report on AI risks and opportunities.

item.title: ‘6.1 coming soon’: Tibo says the Ultrafast speed tier is coming to GPT-6.1 Sol — but there’s no date, no price
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI product lead Tibo Sottiaux told developers on X that ‘6.1 coming soon’ means the Ultrafast speed tier for GPT-6.1 Sol. The paid tier promises about 300 tokens per second in Codex, but OpenAI has announced neither a release date nor a price.

item.title: Give your coding agent real eyes: hands-on with Chrome DevTools MCP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Chrome DevTools MCP (ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp, 53,000+ stars, Apache-2.0) hands your coding agent the keys to a live Chrome browser — screenshots, console messages, network requests, performance traces, and Lighthouse audits. Install it with one command, then let your agent see what it builds.

item.title: Cantina open-sources Apex Flash-1: a 321B-param security model that nearly matches Claude Opus 5 High — for $2.38 instead of $74.68
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cantina Security has released Apex Flash-1, an open-weights RL fine-tune of GLM-5.3-Flash built for vulnerability research. On the company's own held-out test it solved 40 of 60 exploit tasks — just behind Claude Opus 5 High's 43, at a fraction of the estimated run cost.

item.title: Stop tabbing back to the terminal: monitor Claude Code from your Mac's notch — hands-on with Coucou
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Coucou (3,200+ stars, MIT) puts a live companion in your Mac's notch that watches your coding agents — live session steps, file diffs as they happen, and permission approvals with one click. Download it, install the Claude Code hooks, and stop tabbing back to the terminal.

item.title: Altman calls AI ‘religious force’ talk a ‘real safety issue’ — Anthropic is the unspoken target
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wrote on X Saturday that he is “very uncomfortable” with people ascribing “religious force” to AI models or surrendering human judgment to them, calling it “a real safety issue.” Axios read the post as a veiled shot at Anthropic, though Altman named no one.

item.title: Trump picks DNI Jay Clayton as AI czar: the ‘Super Intelligence Force’ has 120 days
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports the White House has created a ‘Super Intelligence Force’ task force to weigh AI’s risks and opportunities and recommend the federal government’s role — led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, with a report due within 120 days.

item.title: Stop burning tokens on grep: find code by asking what it does — hands-on with jevgrep
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: jevgrep (dzhng/jevgrep, 2,100+ stars, MIT) turns repo questions into source excerpts: ask what the code does, Jev judges relevance, your coding agent gets a place to start. Install it, authenticate, install the skill, and stop burning tokens on grep.

item.title: OpenAI safety veteran quits, says the culture is broken: 'the time for trial and error is over'
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: David Robinson spent 3½ years on OpenAI's safety side, helped draft its preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. In an essay published October 3, he says the company's sprint culture can't deliver the care advanced AI demands: “the time for trial and error is over.”

item.title: PriceLabs launches Athena: a proactive AI revenue analyst that flags pricing mistakes before they cost you
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: PriceLabs launched Athena on October 3: a proactive AI revenue analyst for vacation rentals that runs deterministic pricing agents and scheduled routines across a portfolio, flags problems with evidence, and recommends pricing actions the owner can accept, review, or reject. Nothing changes until the user accepts.

item.title: Prime Intellect launches Prime Inference: serverless and reserved GPU serving for open models, tuned for 100 tok/s agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Prime Intellect launched Prime Inference: serverless endpoints and reserved capacity for frontier open models on its own NVIDIA Blackwell fleet, tuned for agentic workloads at 100 tokens per second per user.

item.title: Give your AI agent eyes on the whole internet: hands-on with Agent Reach, the 89K-star toolkit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Agent Reach (89K+ stars, MIT) gives any coding agent read-and-search access to X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and more — one CLI, zero API fees. Install it, run agent-reach doctor, and put the social internet behind a single command.

item.title: Springer retracts a peer-reviewed AI review over undeclared generative AI — the citations gave it away
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Discover Artificial Intelligence, a Springer Nature journal, has retracted a 2024 review on AI in communication research after concluding it was written with undeclared generative AI. The giveaway was the references: contextually wrong citations, the classic fingerprint of machine-generated scholarship.

item.title: Free Gemini = Flash-Lite only: Google moves Flash and Pro behind paywalls on October 9
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's updated support docs say free-tier users lose the Flash and Pro models on October 9 and keep only Flash-Lite. AI Plus loses Pro too; paid Pro and Ultra tiers gain Deep Think.

item.title: Make your coding agent talk like a caveman: a hands-on guide to cutting its token bill
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: caveman (109K stars, Apache-2.0) teaches your coding agent to talk like a caveman: a one-command skill trims its output, a local proxy shrinks what it reads before every call — measured at -33.2% input tokens, red rows and all. The hands-on setup.

item.title: Kolibri has landed: Aleph Alpha drops a 78B open-weight German/English model — Apache 2.0, trained in the EU
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri on October 3: a 78B-parameter mixture-of-experts model for German and English, open-weight under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, trained from scratch in Germany and Finland.

item.title: Stop your coding agent trusting stale docs: a hands-on guide to seiso
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: seiso (MIT, ~170 stars) is a Markdown convention and linter built for docs written by AI and read by humans and agents. Install it, declare each document's kind, hook it into Claude Code — and make stale docs fail loudly.

item.title: FieldAI lands $700M at a $10B valuation: the mapless robot-brain startup 5x'd in a year
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Business Insider reports the Irvine robot-software startup closed a $700M Series C at a $10B valuation — five times its 2025 mark — on mapless navigation that already earns $135M across 30+ customers.

item.title: Read arXiv papers like a well-typeset book: a hands-on guide to EasyRead
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: EasyRead (MIT, 600+ stars) re-typesets any PDF into a bilingual book on your own machine — formulas and tables intact, AI answers in the margin, and a CLI your coding agents can drive. The hands-on setup.
